# Daza et al. — Basin Entropy (2016)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** Alvar Daza et al., “Basin Entropy: A New Tool to Analyze Uncertainty in Dynamical Systems,” *Scientific Reports* 6 (2016): 31416, https://doi.org/10.1038/srep31416.

**Shortened note:** Daza et al., “Basin Entropy.”

**Bibliography:** Daza, Alvar, Alexandre Wagemakers, Bertrand Georgeot, David Guéry-Odelin, and Miguel A. F. Sanjuán. “Basin Entropy: A New Tool to Analyze Uncertainty in Dynamical Systems.” *Scientific Reports* 6 (2016): 31416. https://doi.org/10.1038/srep31416.

## Essay use

Daza et al. provides a controlled technical definition of a basin of attraction and a direct scope condition for when attractor/basin language applies. It can discipline the dynamical vocabulary in §2/#4, not transfer a mathematical basin into psyche, QL, life, or machine subjectivity.

**Claim boundary:** it neither establishes the essay’s dia/sym pulse nor supplies a theory of bifurcation, Jungian complexes, metaphysical identity, consciousness, intentionality, life, or AI subjectivity.

## Passage card — `daza-et-al-2016-basin-entropy-q002` — applicability limit
^daza-et-al-2016-basin-entropy-q002

> “The previous discussion applies typically to dissipative dynamical systems. However, for open Hamiltonian systems, where the concept of attractors or basins of attraction is meaningless, we can still define escape basins in an analogous way to the basins of attraction in a dissipative system.”

- **Locator:** Introduction, immediately following the basin definition.
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manually transcribed from the publisher HTML version of record; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
